q: Which is the largest continent by area?
e: Asia is the largest continent, covering about 30% of the world's land.

q: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
e: The Sahara in North Africa is the largest hot desert.

q: The Equator does NOT pass through which of these countries?
e: The Equator passes through Brazil, Kenya and Indonesia; India lies entirely north of it.

q: Which strait separates Asia from North America?
e: The Bering Strait lies between Russia (Asia) and Alaska (North America).

q: Which country is known as the 'Land of the Rising Sun'?
e: Japan's name 'Nippon' means 'origin of the sun'.

q: The deepest known point in the oceans lies in the:
e: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench (Pacific Ocean) is the deepest point.

q: The Prime Meridian (0° longitude) passes through:
e: The Prime Meridian passes through the Royal Observatory at Greenwich, London.

q: Which is the smallest continent by area?
e: Australia is the smallest continent.

q: Mount Kilimanjaro is located in:
e: Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest peak, is in northern Tanzania.

q: The Great Barrier Reef lies off the coast of:
e: The Great Barrier Reef is off Queensland in north-east Australia.

q: The Andes mountains are in which continent?
e: The Andes run along the western side of South America.

q: Which is the largest island in the world?
e: Greenland is the largest island; Australia is counted as a continent.

q: Which river carries the largest volume of water (discharge) in the world?
e: The Amazon has by far the greatest discharge of any river.

q: The Strait of Gibraltar connects:
e: The Strait of Gibraltar lies between Spain and Morocco, joining the Atlantic and the Mediterranean.

q: The Suez Canal connects:
e: The Suez Canal in Egypt links the Mediterranean with the Red Sea.

q: The ozone layer is found mainly in which layer of the atmosphere?
e: Most ozone is in the stratosphere, where it absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays.

q: The Atacama Desert, one of the driest places on Earth, is in:
e: The Atacama lies in northern Chile along the Pacific coast.

q: Lake Baikal, the deepest lake in the world, is in:
e: Lake Baikal is in Siberia, Russia.

q: The International Date Line roughly follows which meridian?
e: The Date Line runs roughly along the 180° meridian in the Pacific Ocean.

q: The 'Doldrums', a belt of calm winds, lie near the:
e: The Doldrums are a low-pressure belt of calm air near the Equator.

q: The Black Forest is a mountain region in:
e: The Black Forest (Schwarzwald) is in south-west Germany.

q: Victoria Falls lies on which river?
e: Victoria Falls is on the Zambezi, on the Zambia-Zimbabwe border.

q: 'Chinook' is a warm local wind that blows in the:
e: The Chinook blows down the eastern slopes of the Rockies and melts snow quickly.

q: The 'Pampas' grasslands are found in:
e: The Pampas are temperate grasslands of Argentina; the Veld is in South Africa.

q: Which is the longest mountain range on land in the world?
e: The Andes stretch about 7,000 km along South America.

q: Lines on a map joining places of equal rainfall are called:
e: Isohyets join equal rainfall; isotherms join equal temperature and isobars equal pressure.

q: The Kalahari Desert lies mainly in which country?
e: Most of the Kalahari Desert is in Botswana, extending into Namibia and South Africa.

q: The Mohorovicic (Moho) discontinuity separates the:
e: The Moho marks the boundary between Earth's crust and mantle; the Gutenberg discontinuity separates mantle and core.

q: The Dardanelles strait connects the Sea of Marmara with the:
e: The Dardanelles links the Sea of Marmara to the Aegean Sea; the Bosporus links Marmara to the Black Sea.

q: Which river crosses the Equator twice?
e: The Congo river crosses the Equator twice as it curves through Central Africa.
